newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil labor group proposes shorter work week.
newsitem.headline: Brazil labor group proposes shorter work week.

text.p: Brazil's biggest trade union group, the Single Workers Confederation (CUT), proposed Wednesday a cut in the work week, which it said would generate more than three million new jobs.

CUT president Vicente Paulo da Silva met with President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to explain the proposal for a maximum 40-hour working week, down from 44 hours as stipulated in Brazil's constitution.

"We have to work less so we can all work," the document said. CUT estimates that 9.5 million of Brazil's total population of about 160 million are unemployed and that 15.5 million work in the informal sector.
Brazil's official unemployment rate is about five percent.
By cutting the working week to 40 from 44 hours, the government would create 3.6 million new jobs, CUT said.
It also said Brazilian productivity levels had risen by 45 percent between 1990 and 1996, mainly through the use of overtime, but that no benefits of the increase had been passed on to workers.
